messages:
miriam: Heads-up: DAST flagged what looks like a session token in an outgoing webhook payload from staging. Only reproduces ~30% of runs. Attaching logs below. @sec-bot did you also see this? :eyes:

sec-bot: automated-scan: DAST high - session-token-in-body for https://hooks.internal.example.com/notify - evidence attached. scan_id: daf-7c3b. Recommend triage.

raj: ack. Can you paste the exact header/body snippet?

miriam: sure, sanitized:```
POST /notify HTTP/1.1
Host: hooks.internal.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"user_id":"u-123","session":"sess_eyJhbGci...","event":"order.created"}
```

miriam: note: the token looks like a short-lived session token (not API key). We rotated the webhook service account last week — possible correlation.

leo: interesting. KMS audit shows a flurry of decrypts from the webhook service principal around 2026-02-12T14:02Z — looks like token minting. Could be duplicated due to retry logic?

ada: could this be a misconfigured header mapping sending the encrypted token in cleartext to the webhook? i.e., we call encrypt(session) -> we should send ciphertext, but maybe middleware is calling decrypt() before forwarding.

sam: if middleware accidentally decrypts, that would explain plaintext leakage. Any commit/rollout around that time? @miriam when did staging deploy last week?

miriam: staging deploys: prod-like rollout at 2026-02-12 13:55Z. Relevant PR: gh#4228 (webhook/middleware change).

raj: quick repro plan: 1) replay failing DAST job in staging 2) capture full outgoing webhook 3) correlate with KMS decrypt logs and service principal id. Anyone can take step 1 now?

leo: I can do step 3 and pull KMS logs. Give me the job id.

miriam: job id: ci-dast-1729. Replaying now.

miriam: replayed. Confirmed outgoing payload contains plaintext session token in 3/10 attempts.

leo: KMS logs show decrypts at the same times as those 3 attempts, principal: svc-webhook@infra. Looks like middleware is calling keystore.Decrypt() and attaching result.

ada: that matches my hypothesis. So root cause: middleware change in gh#4228 added an automatic session lookup/decrypt and a mis-scoped flag toggled it on for webhooks.

sam: mitigation options: A) revoke short-lived sessions (force logout) B) revert middleware flag C) update webhook to strip session fields before forwarding D) block outbound webhooks until fix. Thoughts?

raj: prioritize low-impact: roll back the flag (B) in staging and prod if we see signs in prod. But we should also rotate any sessions that leaked. Are there live tokens tied to user sessions?

miriam: leaked tokens are short-lived (1h) but could be used. We should rotate affected sessions and add a quick detection rule.

leo: I can add a KMS-based alert: if Decrypt() calls originate from svc-webhook principal and target key == session-key, raise high-priority alert.

ada: +1. Also add an outbound filter at the edge to redact fields named "session" or matching pattern sess_.* for now. That reduces blast radius immediately.

sam: will open a quick PR to add redaction middleware at the egress layer. Mark it hotfix.

miriam: assigning ownership: sam will PR edge-redact, raj will roll back the flag if needed, leo will add KMS alert, ada will update runbook and escalate timeline, i'll coordinate session rotation and user notifications (if required).

sam: PR opened: gh#4251 - edge redact middleware. Short patch, tests included.

raj: flag rollback patch ready in staging pipeline, will cut if we see any sign in prod.

leo: KMS alert created: rule id kms-alert-493. Test firing simulated.

ada: runbook note draft: add triage steps for webhook plaintext leaks, owner role, and RBAC check for service principals that can call Decrypt(). Putting in runbook PR now.

miriam: we should also check audit logging: does keystore.Decrypt() show request origin IP/trace id? If not, we need to extend audit to include trace_id for forensic correlation.

leo: current audit has principal and key_id but not trace_id. I'll file an infra ticket to add request.trace_id to keystore audit events. gh#4260.

sec-bot: incident-notice: potential PII/session leak; severity: high -> triage channel: eng-security. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-119.

sam: good catch. Also: update CI SAST/DAST test harness to fuzz for tokens in outbound payloads so this doesn't pass silently. I'll add a small post-run check that scans outgoing webhooks for high-entropy token patterns.

miriam: estimated timeline: edge redaction and runbook updates today (2-3h). KMS audit change and session rotation next 24h. Prod rollback only if we detect similar patterns in prod.

raj: action items summarized: - sam: PR edge redact (gh#4251) - leo: KMS alert + file audit enhancement (kms-alert-493, gh#4260) - raj: rollback plan ready - ada: runbook PR & RBAC review - miriam: session rotation + incident comms - all: monitor DAST jobs for 24h

miriam: thanks all. Please react with :white_check_mark: when you complete your task.

sam: :white_check_mark: PR merged to staging, deploying now.

leo: :white_check_mark: alert in place, simulated fire.

ada: :white_check_mark: runbook PR opened gh#4264.

raj: standing by for prod signal.

miriam: closing loop: no production evidence found after 24h, sessions rotated proactively, audits queued. Closing incident draft and will post a short postmortem in #postmortems tomorrow. :lock:
